narrative.overview: A clean government counter at a visa-processing office: precise paperwork, calm process, no wasted ink. Every screen is a desk surface — white paper laid flat on a neutral band, enclosed by a hairline stroke instead of a shadow, and labeled by a system that speaks in small, exact captions. The palette is intentionally monochrome: near-black ink is the only element that ever fills a surface, while color appears exclusively and sparingly inside tinted status pills. The interface feels confident, orderly, and unhurried — officialese without oppressive density.
keyCharacteristics: Grayscale OKLCH system; color reserved for status pills and destructive relief
Hairline-outline depth (never drop shadows); glow belongs to focus rings only
Compact, procedural controls (32px) with strong primary-ink fills
Passport numbers set in Geist Mono like official serial stamps
Tinted status windows: ~15% fill behind the hue's 600-step text at medium weight
Fully supported dark mode (system default, class attribute, Ctrl+D toggle)

rules.name: The Ink-Only Primary Rule
rules.body: The palette's only filled element is near-black ink. No brand hue, no colored buttons; rarity IS the discipline.

rules.name: The Tint-Window Rule
rules.body: Status hues live in one shape only: a pill with ~15% tinted background and the hue's 600-step text at medium weight. Never solid fills, never colored borders.

rules.name: The One-Status Pill Rule
rules.body: A passport carries at most one status tint and one payment tint; two pills max on any record row.

rules.name: The Serial-Stencil Rule
rules.body: Any identifier printed on the physical document — passport numbers — is set in Geist Mono (14px/600). No other text uses mono.

rules.name: The Focus-Glow Exception
rules.body: The focus-visible ring (3px, ring/50%) is the one place light blooms. Hover states stay flat; nothing floats, nothing drops a shadow.

dos: Do keep all surfaces flat: white paper, hairline ring strokes (ring-1 ring-foreground/10 / border-input), Paper Gray hover fills.
Do confine every chroma to a pill: ~15% tinted window + the hue's 600-step hue text at medium weight (blue/600, amber/600, emerald/600), or destructive/10 + Rejection Red.
Do set passport numbers in Geist Mono at 14px/600 — the serial stamp treatment.
Do keep interactive controls at 32px with 10px radius and a 3px focus ring glow; label every field in 12px/500 muted caption.
Do align forms on the 2-col/4-col responsive grids with 16px gaps; align table headers uppercase with wide tracking.
Do maintain dispatches for dark mode (class strategy): tinted borders and surface contrast stand in for every light-mode hairline.
donts: Don't drop shadows for depth — ring strokes only; the focus ring is the sole glow.
Don't color buttons, inputs, or backgrounds with palette hues; Desk Ink is the only fill.
Don't use solid status fills or colored borders for status information.
Don't put more than two status pills on one record row (one status + one payment).
Don't apply the pill (26px radius) to anything except badges; controls stay rectangular at their scale step.
Don't uppercase body text or headings — the uppercase voice belongs to table headers and 12px labels only.
